summary:
**R6 is a viable design seam, with the corrections below required before implementation closure.** Reviewed `59fac274a5` read-only. No edits, builds, tests, jobs, or browser actions were performed. This provides no production activation approval.

1. **Require pairing by construction; forbid projection attachment or replacement.**  
   Preserve `SourceResourceContext::new` and its existing downcast behavior. Add a constructor shaped as `new_accounted<T: Any + Send + Sync + AllocationAccount>(Arc<T>)`, internally deriving both erased payload and account projection from that one argument. Fields remain private; no constructor accepting two independent Arcs, setter, attachment method, or user-supplied projection closure.

   This addresses the parent’s forgery concern: an attach API could preserve a valid private-`Inner` payload while substituting another accounting backend. A generic paired constructor preserves allocation identity without registries or raw retained authority. The public, downstream-implementable trait remains a resource interface; it grants no source authority.

   Relevant current seam: [resource_context.rs](/home/louistrue/.t3/worktrees/ifc-lite/t3-f778e361/rust/core/src/execution_owner/resource_context.rs:10), [account.rs](/home/louistrue/.t3/worktrees/ifc-lite/t3-f778e361/rust/geometry/src/resource/account.rs:39).

2. **Make fault propagation complete, including early account failures.**  
   Current prototype gate paths return directly from `backend.check()?`. Adding a captured observer only to admission failures or `record` would leave cancellation and previously established account faults unobserved.

   Every gate entry, operation check, admission refusal, overflow, and Global failure must select and propagate through the same explicit channels: original source stop first, account first fault second, captured terminal third. Preserve the account’s own first fault even when an ancestor source stop takes reporting precedence. Cleanup refunds bypass work admission and remain available after every terminal state.

   New `Inner` admission must check cancellation and terminal state under the same `State` lock used to commit counters. Do not implement it by calling public `prepare`, which routes errors through ambient `stop`.

3. **Remove cross-channel calls and destruction from locked regions.**  
   [OwnedResourceContext::remember](/home/louistrue/.t3/worktrees/ifc-lite/t3-f778e361/rust/geometry/src/resource/owned.rs:36) currently holds the terminal mutex while checking/stopping source and account channels. It cannot serve unchanged as the direct observer. Snapshot local terminal state, release the lock, consult/update the other channels, then commit the selected terminal without holding another channel’s lock.

   There is another destructor-sensitive seam: [ExecutionSourceScope::drop](/home/louistrue/.t3/worktrees/ifc-lite/t3-f778e361/rust/core/src/execution_owner.rs:260) replaces `active_source` while holding its mutex, dropping the displaced context there. Final account destruction can release a `PoolPermit` and enter the pool mutex. Move the displaced value out under lock and destroy it afterward. Apply the same discipline to new projection and observer fields.

4. **Specify metadata envelopes by retained backing, not active operations.**  
   The proposed same-account metadata admission is necessary, but production sizing is unresolved. Four gates and sixteen frames/ancestors cannot become acceptance limits without workload authority; existing epoch validation has no corresponding depth cap.

   Define separately the bounds and lifetimes for retained gates, observer state, owner state, epochs, binding frames, and any adapter record. Ending work does not necessarily release backing: allocator-bearing containers, dormant continuations, and weak references can retain it. Metadata admission must precede allocation, unwind on construction failure, and refund only at the backing’s actual destruction point.

   Keep the pre-existing account allocation explicitly declared as baseline. Avoid storing a strong account reference inside account-owned metadata merely to fund itself. A gate retaining the account and weakly referencing `SourceBundle` is compatible with the intended ownership graph.

5. **Make category accounting atomic and prevent migration double charges.**  
   Add tracked-layout live bytes as a checked subset of the existing total under `State`; both must change atomically. Refund validates category and total before subtraction, after Global free, and cannot panic or allocate. Growth admits the full new layout while old backing remains charged. Global failure rolls back provisional live bytes only; admitted cumulative work/copy and peak history remain.

   Existing `Reservation::retain` and `reserve_headers` conservatively retain charges. When those containers later acquire allocator ownership, remove or explicitly partition their old backing charges in the same migration. Otherwise the same storage is charged twice. Preserve existing `prepare_inner` admission semantics for current callers.

6. **Separate the cross-crate account seam from prototype activation.**  
   The allocator backend and authority prototype currently compile only under core’s `cfg(test)` plus feature. Geometry dependency builds cannot implement a trait hidden there. Put the minimal account trait and paired constructor in the dependency-visible API boundary; keep projection extraction and tracked constructors private to core.

   Keep `ProductOwner` activation coordinated separately. Preserve the original private-`Inner` downcast used by joined workers in [with_source_resources](/home/louistrue/.t3/worktrees/ifc-lite/t3-f778e361/rust/processing/src/element/session_canonical.rs:85). Absence of a projection must never silently select ambient accounting for tracked work.

The concrete next implementation seam is the paired context constructor, direct `Inner` account methods, and direct captured-terminal observer, while leaving decoder/cache activation untouched. Core’s opted-in unit-test target can exercise the real geometry account through its existing geometry dev-dependency without exposing tracked constructors.

That boundary does **not** complete owner/cache/Raw migration. Public cache extraction/import, decoded-entity ownership, nested attribute storage, shared lazy caches, retained receipts, and Raw-region resource capture still require coherent ownership migration. Generation-coupled revision witnessing remains insufficient as complete cache authority. Exact/default behavior must remain supported throughout; neither the prior prototype results nor this review closes those obligations.
